rules.title: Container runs as root
rules.why: A root process in a container turns any code-execution flaw into full container control and widens the blast radius of a runtime escape.
rules.falsePositiveHints: A USER root during a build stage followed by a non-root USER for runtime is fine. Check the final stage.

rules.title: No non-root USER declared in the Dockerfile
rules.why: Without a USER instruction the container runs as root by default.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Some base images already set a non-root user. Check the FROM image before reporting.

rules.title: Unpinned base image or build secret in a layer
rules.why: An unpinned base image makes builds non-reproducible and silently pulls new content. A secret in ENV/ARG persists in the image layers and in docker history, even if later removed.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Separate the two: unpinned image is A08/Medium; a real secret value in a layer is A02/Critical. Only flag ARG/ENV that carries an actual value, not a name awaiting injection.

rules.title: Privileged or over-permissive pod security context
rules.why: A privileged container shares the host kernel namespace boundary in name only; escape to the node is straightforward.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Genuine infrastructure DaemonSets (CNI, storage, monitoring agents) may legitimately require this. Judge by workload type.

rules.title: Kubernetes Secret with an inline value
rules.why: base64 in a Secret manifest is encoding, not encryption. A committed manifest is a committed secret.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Sealed Secrets, External Secrets Operator references and SOPS-encrypted files are correct patterns and not findings.

rules.title: Terraform resource open to the internet or publicly readable
rules.why: 0.0.0.0/0 ingress and public object ACLs are among the most common causes of real-world data exposure.
rules.falsePositiveHints: 0.0.0.0/0 on port 443 for a public load balancer is intended. On 22, 3389, or a database port it is a finding. Check the port.

rules.title: Terraform variable or output holding a secret in plaintext
rules.why: A default value for a secret ends up in state files and plan output, both of which are frequently stored unencrypted.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Verify the variable actually holds a credential rather than a name or ARN.

rules.title: Environment file committed to the repository
rules.why: A committed .env is a committed credential set, and it stays in git history after deletion.
rules.falsePositiveHints: .env.example / .env.template with placeholder values is correct practice. Check whether the value is real. Also check .gitignore - an untracked .env present on disk is a different (and much lower) finding than a tracked one.

rules.title: CI workflow with a risky trigger or an inline secret
rules.why: pull_request_target runs untrusted fork code with repository secrets in scope - a well-known supply-chain compromise path. Inline secrets in CI config leak to every build log.
rules.falsePositiveHints: ${{ secrets.NAME }} references are correct and not findings. pull_request_target without a checkout of the PR head is safe; check what the job checks out.

rules.title: Unpinned third-party CI action or script piped to a shell
rules.why: A mutable tag or a curl-to-shell install means the code executed in your pipeline can change without any change to your repository.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Actions pinned to a full commit SHA are correct. First-party actions from your own org are lower risk but still mutable.

rules.title: Application configuration weakening a security control
rules.why: Debug compilation, disabled request validation and verbose errors in a deployed configuration each hand an attacker information or remove a control.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Check whether the file is a Development-only overlay (appsettings.Development.json) that production never loads.

rules.title: Sensitive path not excluded from version control
rules.why: Without ignore rules, a secret file is one `git add .` away from permanent history.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Only relevant if such files actually exist or are likely in this stack. Do not report on a repository with no secret-bearing file types.
